claim.quote: together the data yield a muon lifetime of tau_{mu}(MuLan) = 2196980.3(2.2) ps (1.0 ppm), thirty times more precise than previous generations of lifetime experiments.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; the journal version is Phys. Rev. D 87, 052003 (2013).

key_value_text.quote: The lifetime measurement yields the most accurate value of the Fermi constant G_F (MuLan) = 1.1663787(6) x 10^{-5} GeV^{-2} (0.5 ppm).

name: Detailed Report of the MuLan Measurement of the Positive Muon Lifetime and Determination of the Fermi Constant

significance.quote: The lifetime measurement yields the most accurate value of the Fermi constant G_F (MuLan) = 1.1663787(6) x 10^{-5} GeV^{-2} (0.5 ppm).
significance.value: Lifetime 1.0 ppm; Fermi constant to 0.5 ppm

summary.plain: The full write-up of the MuLan measurement. About 1.6 trillion decay positrons from two target setups give the same muon lifetime, and the Fermi constant to 0.5 parts per million.
summary.technical: Detailed report: ~1.6 x 10^12 positrons with a magnetized ferromagnetic target (~4 kG) and a crystal quartz target (130 G); tau(MuLan) = 2196980.3(2.2) ps (1.0 ppm); G_F(MuLan) = 1.1663787(6) x 10^-5 GeV^-2 (0.5 ppm).

title: Detailed Report of the MuLan Measurement of the Positive Muon Lifetime and Determination of the Fermi Constant
why_it_matters: The abstract says the lifetime measurement yields the most accurate value of the Fermi constant and enables new precision studies of weak interactions via lifetime measurements of muonic atoms.
